precepts.text: When Jesus therefore perceived that they would come and take him by force, to make him a king, he departed again into a mountain himself alone. That is how much Israel loved him: they said, we want him to be our king. He said no, because there would be no more king until Christ returns.
precepts.point: From the sit down: one of the pastors said there was a curse on Jeconiah that nobody of his seed would sit as king, so the genealogy is ruled out. Think: after Jeconiah, was there a king in Israel sitting on the throne? No. When Babylon came in, that was it; Zedekiah came, and they killed him with his sons. There was no king during the time of Christ, because the prophets said there would be no more king until Christ returns.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
Matthew traces the line “after they were brought to Babylon”: Jechonias begat Salathiel, Salathiel begat Zorobabel, and on down to “Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” That is the Branch, right through Zerubbabel.

In the sit down with Captain Matathias and Captain Galiah, the dude with that stupid hat said there was a curse on Jeconiah that nobody of his seed would sit as king, so the genealogy is ruled out. Think. After Jeconiah, was there a king in Israel sitting on the throne? No. When Babylon came in, that was it. Zedekiah came, and they got rid of him and killed him with his sons. There was no king during the time of Christ.

John shows it: “When Jesus therefore perceived that they would come and take him by force, to make him a king, he departed again into a mountain himself alone.” That is how much Israel loved him. They said, we want him to be our king. He said no.

Why? Because the prophets said there would be no more king until Christ returns. The sceptre was held for Shiloh, the Messiah, “and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.” Christ would not be made king by force before the time, so the line through Jeconiah and Zerubbabel is not ruled out; it runs straight to the one king still to sit on the throne.

precepts.text: I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger.
precepts.point: First the weekly Sabbath, whose true meaning we just read: rest going into the kingdom. Then the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord's passover, which we just finished celebrating, and the fifteenth day begins the feast of unleavened bread: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread. The unleavened bread is Christ's sinless life, and the haste out of Egypt besides.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
After passover comes the next feast: “on the fifteenth day of the same month is the feast of unleavened bread unto the Lord: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread.” There is that seven again.

The unleavened bread represents Christ: his sinless life, not having leaven. We know the history too, the Most High wanted us to hurry up and leave Egypt, so there was no time to sit and bake bread. But it also goes into Christ’s unleavened life, sinless and blameless.

Christ says it: “I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger”. He is the bread of life, the unleavened bread of the feast.

precepts.text: It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing. The words I speak unto you are spirit and life.
precepts.point: The camp is not small any more. A brother making a delivery in another state got recognized by someone outside the truth. If he had been doing wickedness, that is how easily it gets found out.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

precepts.why:
“It is the spirit that quickeneth”: only the spirit can change you as a man. “the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.” So when Galatians says walk in the Spirit, it means walk in the words of Christ, the laws, statutes and commandments, and you will not fulfil the lust of the flesh.

Those words have to live in you. The Bible should be like the receptionist at the front desk of an office building: nobody gets in unless she lets them. The door to your soul is your forehead, so the Bible should sit there. When the plan comes up, it says, I hear you, but that's two to five; that's ten to fifteen; that's life. Thou shalt not steal.

When you see a beautiful woman and are tempted to start rubbernecking, you remember Job: I made a covenant with my eyes, why then should I think upon a maid? If you walk in a place and there's a stack of money with nobody around, thou shalt not steal. Without the scriptures readily in your mind, it is impossible not to fall into temptation.

And hidden wickedness does not stay hidden. We are not small any more. A brother making a delivery from another state was recognized by someone not even in the truth. Imagine if he had been doing wickedness. The words of Christ are spirit and life; the flesh profits nothing.

precepts.point: Thus Nehemiah cleansed the people from all strangers, appointed the wards of the priests and Levites every one in his business, and provided for the wood offering and the firstfruits, closing the book with the prayer, Remember me, O my God, for good. This is the book of records, and to see it as history rather than religion is to understand who these people are.

note.label: Nehemiah 13: Cleansing the People, the Sabbath, and the Strange Wives

precepts.why:
Nehemiah chased away the son of Joiada who was son in law to Sanballat the Horonite, because the priesthood and its covenant had been defiled, and “Thus cleansed I them from all strangers”. This is the book of records, and to see it as history rather than religion is to understand who these people are.

Christ says, “No man can come to me, except the Father which hath sent me draw him: and I will raise him up at the last day.” No man can come to the Most High except the Father draw him, and he draws him when he hears the words of this Bible. That is why the sheep hear his voice and a stranger they will not follow.

The strangers Nehemiah cleansed out had no part in the covenant of the priesthood. Those who are drawn by the Father hear these words and know their own history in them, and it is those he will raise up at the last day. Nehemiah closes his book asking, “Remember me, O my God, for good.”

precepts.why:
Some of us know and believe the end is coming. Some of us are just hoping the end is coming. And some are just here in unbelief abiding: abiding time for a job, or a spouse, whichever comes first, and then we will never see you again, and God won't see you any more either. The ones that are only here for a spouse are the ones that can't wait for the proving process, six months to a year; they do the back-door marriage. Some of them used to sit right here; now they went to another camp and got another man, measuring tape and all.

“When the people therefore saw that Jesus was not there, neither his disciples, they also took shipping, and came to Capernaum, seeking for Jesus. And when they had found him on the other side of the sea, they said unto him, Rabbi,” Rabbi means master. “when camest thou hither? Jesus answered them and said, Verily, verily, I say unto you,” Listen good to what Christ says to these people that were looking so desperately for him, like they believed. “Ye seek me, not because ye saw the miracles, but because ye did eat of the loaves, and were filled.” Christ cut them sharp: some of you only seek me not because of the miracles but because you got food; you got fed, and that is why you follow me. Believe it or not, some of us listening right now, in here or online, are only following because there is some benefit you are looking for, whether it be food, a job or a spouse. One of those three things.

“Labour not for the meat which perisheth,” Labour means to work; don't work and strive for the meat that perishes. “but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life,” The meat that endures unto everlasting life is the word of God, the commandments. “which the Son of man shall give unto you: for him hath God the Father sealed.” Some people, men and women, will only love you as much as they can use you; their loyalty ends where the benefits stop. That means you should not have gone on the Quest, because you were not prepared to go. Or they ask for the rent money before, and then go on the Quest after. It is like a pattern we see, and don't think we are simple, we see it, and the Lord sees that too.
